summary: Induction on j: a parabolic matrix for j + 1 is fromBlocks(A, B, 0, D) with A parabolic for j and D ∈ GL_T.

steps.lean:
j.rec ⟨0, by simp!
  [parabolic, BlockTriangular]⟩ fun j ⟨k, H⟩ ↦ ⟨k + Fintype.card (T × BlockIndex N T j), fun R ↦
  have e (u : parabolic (R := R) (@blockNumber N T j.succ)) := (ext fun _ _ ↦ u.2 (by simp!) :
    u.1.1.toBlocks₂₁ = 0) ▸ fromBlocks_toBlocks _
  have d u := isUnit_fromBlocks_zero₂₁'.1 ⟨_, (e u).symm⟩
  by simp [Nat.card_congr (β := parabolic (blockNumber j) × _ × GL T R) (.mk (fun u ↦
       (⟨(d u).1.unit, fun _ _ ↦ (u.2 ·)⟩, _, (d u).2.unit)) (fun (x, y, z) ↦
       ⟨.mk'' (fromBlocks x.1 y 0 z) (by simp!), by simpa! [parabolic, BlockTriangular,
       lt_asymm] using! x.2⟩) (by ext : 2; use e ·)), H, Matrix, Nat.card_pi]
     ring⟩

steps.claim: j = 0: blockNumber is constant, every matrix is block triangular, and k = 0 works.

steps.claim: A matrix u of the parabolic for j + 1 has zero lower-left block (the new copy of T has the highest level), so u = fromBlocks(A, B, 0, D).
steps.lean:
have e (u : parabolic (R := R) (@blockNumber N T j.succ)) := (ext fun _ _ ↦ u.2 (by simp!) :
    u.1.1.toBlocks₂₁ = 0) ▸ fromBlocks_toBlocks _

steps.claim: u ↦ (A, B, D) is a bijection onto (parabolic for j) × Mat(BlockIndex_j × T, R) × GL_T(R), so Nat.card of the parabolic is Nat.card(P_j)·Nat.card(R)^{|BlockIndex_j|·|T|}·Nat.card(GL_T(R)) (Nat.card_congr, Nat.card_pi); with H the formula follows.
